text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Iraqi press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Saddam Hussein chairs cabinet meeting and urges training of state employees.
- Saddam urges giving state employees more incentives to save money in state banks.
- Iraq and United Nations exchange letters on the extention of oil-for-food deal.
- Iraqi customs department prepares border posts with Syria to allow flow of goods into Iraq.
- Ship loaded with sugar arrives at Umm Qasr port in southern Iraq.
- Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz receives Russian oil delegation.
- Preparations under way for the national census due later this year.
(The above were also carried by JUMHOURIYA and QADISSIYA)
- Editorial lambasts United States for unilateral decisions concerning the so-called American strategic interests in the world.
- Commentary says Turkey's invasion of northern Iraq is a failure.
- Harvest campaign continues in southern Iraq.
- Syrian pharmaceutical firms to hold exhibition in Baghdad later this month.
- Turkish incursion of northern Iraq results in tens to casualties in the city of Arabil.
